result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers fix the core problem the same way. They move focus to the first invalid field, connect errors with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, clear stale errors, and stop showing 'Sent' when the request fails. B goes further: it adds a specific party-size range message, ignores whitespace-only names, prevents double submits and colours the failure status red. Neither replaces the bare 'Sent' or the vague 'Required' wording, and A's three role='alert' regions could announce noisily all at once. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is better overall. Both answers move focus to the first invalid field, link errors with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, clear stale errors and stop showing 'Sent' when the server rejects the request. A also adds a specific party-size range message, uses polite live regions instead of several assertive alerts, shows the failure status in red and disables the button while sending. Neither replaces the bare 'Sent' or the generic 'Required' for empty fields.
